items.title: Entrance
items.why: every building has one place a visitor is meant to arrive at
items.how: add_opening(group, side="south", storey=0, kind="double_door") on the entrance axis, then add_canopy(group, side="south", storey=0, width>=8, depth=4..6, height=3.5..4.5, columns=4) — both BEFORE add_curtain_wall, which keeps the door wall as glass

items.title: Stair
items.why: the way up that works with the power off, and the way out in a fire
items.how: add_stair(cell=<a cell in the core>, from_storey=0, to_storey=20, kind="u", width=1.2) — one record per storey: it cuts the floor opening through each slab and adds the rails

items.title: Lift(s)
items.why: a building of three storeys or more is not usable without one
items.how: add_elevator(cell=<a cell in the core, beside the stair>, from_storey=0, to_storey=20, w=1.8, depth=2.0) x 2 — a door on every storey it passes, and the overrun above the top landing

items.title: Second escape stair
items.why: one fire must not close both ways out
items.how: add_fire_escape(group, side="north", storeys=20, width=1.2) — the side OPPOSITE the entrance (which is on the south) and OUTSIDE the facade, bolted to it; a cell inside the plan puts the escape stair in somebody's flat. Then egress_check(max=30)

items.title: Entrance lobby
items.why: the door hands people to the core; without a lobby the door is the queue
items.how: add_room(cell_from, cell_to, storey=0, name="Lobby") on the entrance axis, core at its far end — at least 8 cells across: a luxury lobby is a room, not a corridor

items.title: Corridor / circulation
items.why: rooms reach the core along something, and its width is decided not left over
items.how: layout_floor(cell_from, cell_to, use="residential", corridor_w=1.8) cuts a whole floor, or add_corridor(cell_from, cell_to, width=1.8) one at a time (the block must be wider than the corridor, or it refuses)

items.title: Toilets
items.why: occupancy sets the count; every floor of a public building needs an accessible one
items.how: add_room(..., name="WC") at the core on every floor, then furnish_bathroom(...) — about 1 fixture(s) per floor plus one accessible cubicle 1.5 x 2.2 m

items.title: Roof
items.why: a building without a roof record is a massing study
items.how: draw_box(..., storeys=20, roof="flat") builds it with the shell, or add_roof(cell_from, cell_to, storey=20, kind="flat") on an existing one — then add_parapet(group, height=1.1) and put the terrace ON the deck (roof y + t)

items.title: Parapet / guarding
items.why: an accessible flat roof or a balcony without guarding is not buildable
items.how: add_parapet(group, height=1.1) round the roof edge; guarding_check() proves it

items.title: Roof access: head house + overrun
items.why: a roof deck nobody can reach is a picture
items.how: add_stair(..., to_storey=20) reaches the deck and builds the head house; add_elevator(..., to_storey=20) adds the overrun

items.title: Roof pool
items.why: the pool is the brief
items.how: add_pool(cell_from, cell_to, storey=20, raised="auto", infinity="south") — storey 20 IS the deck of a 20-storey box, raised so the water stands above it, the infinity edge ON the deck edge facing the view

items.title: Floor line on the facade
items.why: a curtain wall hides the slab edge, and the tower then reads as hollow
items.how: add_curtain_wall(walls, storeys) then add_facade_bands(kind="string_course") per glazed storey

items.title: Rooftop plant + lift overrun
items.why: a bare flat roof is the single clearest tell of a model
items.how: add_rooftop_plant(group) puts plant, tank and screen on the core side; the lift overrun is the shaft's own, from add_elevator(..., to_storey=20) — a roof with plant but no overrun says the lifts stop below it

items.title: Approach: path, drive, lighting
items.why: the entrance has to be reached, and be lit; a door onto grass reads as unfinished
items.how: add_road / add_object(kind="path") to the entrance, then add_street_furniture(kind="lamp_post", height=5) every 8-12 m along both edges

items.title: Cycle store
items.why: one space per dwelling, on the ground storey, not through the lobby carpet
items.how: add_room(..., storey=0, name="Cycle store") on the street side

items.title: Refuse store
items.why: the bin route is a plan decision; found later it goes through the lobby
items.how: add_room(..., storey=0, name="Refuse store") with a level route to the kerb, under 25 m

items.title: Parking
items.why: bays and their 6 m aisle are planned together or the aisle never fits
items.how: add_parking(cell_from, cell_to, aisle=6.0) or draw_parking_garage(decks=N); park_cars() fills a few bays for the render

items.title: Balconies
items.why: a residential facade with no balcony reads as an office
items.how: add_balconies(walls, storeys, depth=1.8, railing=True) on the best facade — at least 10 of them; "added 0 balconies, skipped 11 walls" is a refusal, not a result

items.title: Loading bay
items.why: a lorry must never share the arrival route
items.how: a 3.5 x 12 m bay with 12 m of manoeuvring, on the opposite side from the entrance

items.title: Planting clear of the axis
items.why: real trees, one crown apart, 6 m off the entrance axis
items.how: plant_trees(cell_from, cell_to, count, height, model="real") — take the block the tool names if it refuses; never fall through to another tree tool

items.title: Deck furniture
items.why: an empty roof deck reads as a plant deck, whatever the pool cost
items.how: add_beach_set(cells=[four or more deck cells], storey=20) — every piece lands on the deck under it; or add_object(kind="sun_lounger", ...) one at a time

items.title: Finishes
items.why: a luxury request answered in mat_concrete and mat_steel is a grey massing model
items.how: search_materials("marble") for the id, then set_finish(group, floor_material=<library id>, wall_material=<library id>, roof_material=<library id>), or set_material(ids, <library id>) for the rest — a flat mat_ preset is the default, not a finish

from_request.says: roof pool + roof access + roof = flat_deck

building_program.request:
build a building with footprint of 20x20 , 20 stories high . infinity pool on the roof . roof entrance. nice entrace into the building at ground floor . make ground floor glass walls , 2nd floor rough concrete wall  , 3d floor glass walls , 4th rough concrete , repeat this for all floors.

center building at cell fh100

make building look luxurious
